platforms.name: Northflank
platforms.summary: Full-stack container platform. A preview blueprint, built in a visual editor or as JSON kept in Git, builds each pull request or branch and deploys its services, jobs, databases, volumes, secret groups and URLs as an isolated preview environment, on Northflank's cloud or in your own cloud account.
platforms.summary_short: Visual blueprint per PR: services, jobs, fresh or forked databases, scoped secrets and URLs; managed or BYOC

scope.value: Full-stack: services, jobs, databases, volumes, secret groups, URLs
scope.quote: Each preview environment is an isolated instance of your application with its own services, databases, and URLs.

hosting.value: Managed, BYOC in your cloud account, or your own cluster (BYOK)
hosting.quote: Bring your own cloud (BYOC) runs Northflank workloads in your cloud account...You can also import an existing Kubernetes cluster (BYOK) for Northflank to manage.

git.value: GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Azure DevOps; self-hosted GitLab, GHES, Gitea, Forgejo
git.quote: Northflank integrates with GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Azure DevOps, and Cursor Origin to build and deploy code from your repositories.

trigger.value: PR, push, PR label, check suite, release, cron, webhook, API or manual run
trigger.quote: Preview blueprints can create or update environments from Git events, webhook requests, or a schedule.

databases.value: Fresh database per preview, forked from a snapshot, seeded by a job, or shared
databases.quote: Build your application, provision a fresh database for the preview, deploy the application, and inject the database credentials....Alternatively, fork your database from a snapshot to restore pre-seeded data more efficiently.

cleanup.value: On PR close or branch delete, plus optional expiry (resets on update) and teardown steps
cleanup.quote: Git providers can also request preview deletion when a pull request closes or its branch is deleted.

access.value: Per-port IP policies, basic auth or SSO
access.quote: To configure a port-wide security policy, expand the custom domains & security rules menu for a port and add a new IP policy, credentials, or select an organisation for SSO access control.

license.note: Closed-source commercial service; no open-source license is published.

pricing.value: Previews billed as normal per-second compute; free Sandbox tier
pricing.quote: Up to $20 a month of free resources on Northflank Cloud, across 2 services, 2 jobs, and 1 database.

on_demand_triggers.value: PR label, webhook, API, cron, manual run
on_demand_triggers.quote: Starts a preview run for a pull request with matching labels...Starts a preview run on a UTC schedule...Starts a preview run from a GET or POST request

data_copy.value: Fork a database from a snapshot
data_copy.quote: Alternatively, fork your database from a snapshot to restore pre-seeded data more efficiently.

teardown_hooks.value: Teardown specification runs on preview deletion
teardown_hooks.quote: Add a teardown specification for cleanup when a preview environment is deleted. Use it for external resources or cleanup jobs that normal preview deletion does not handle.

multi_repo.value: Multiple Git triggers and build nodes in one blueprint
multi_repo.quote: This request sets `frontend` to branch `feature` and `backend` to branch `develop`

caveats: Active hours (pause previews outside working hours, resume in the morning) is only available for projects in your own cloud account (https://northflank.com/docs/v1/application/release/set-up-preview-blueprints).

A teardown specification can clean up external resources, such as OpenTofu-managed infrastructure, when a preview is deleted (https://northflank.com/docs/v1/application/release/set-up-preview-blueprints).

With GitOps and 'use branch contents', each preview runs the blueprint file from its own branch, so a PR can change its own preview infrastructure (https://northflank.com/docs/v1/application/release/set-up-preview-blueprints).
A message node can comment the preview URL on the pull request, or post it to Slack or a webhook (https://northflank.com/docs/v1/application/infrastructure-as-code/template-nodes).
Webhook-triggered previews: anyone with the webhook URL can request a preview run, so treat it as a credential (https://northflank.com/docs/v1/application/release/set-up-preview-blueprints).

platforms.name: Vercel
platforms.summary: Managed frontend cloud that builds an immutable preview deployment, with its own URL, for every push to a non-production branch, every pull request, or every CLI deploy without --prod.
platforms.summary_short: Preview deployment per push/PR for frontends and serverless functions

scope.value: Frontend + serverless functions
scope.quote: When you deploy your application, Vercel automatically sets up the tools and optimizations for your chosen framework. It ensures low latency by routing traffic through Vercel's CDN, and placing your functions in a specific region when you need more control over data locality.

hosting.quote: Preview environments allow you to deploy and test changes in a live setting, without affecting your production site.

git.value: GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Origin, Azure Pipelines; CLI for others
git.quote: Vercel allows for automatic deployments on every branch push and merges onto the production branch of your GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Origin, and Azure DevOps Pipelines projects.

trigger.value: Any non-production branch push, PR, or CLI deploy
trigger.quote: Push a commit to a branch that is not your production branch (commonly main)...Create a pull request (PR) on GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, or Origin

databases.value: Per-preview Neon branch via Marketplace integration
databases.quote: Connects your Vercel project to your Neon database to create a database branch for each preview deployment.

cleanup.value: Retention policy: previews deleted after 180 days (Pro) / 30 days (Hobby)
cleanup.quote: | Hobby | 30 days | 30 days | 30 days | 30 days | ... | Pro and Enterprise | 30 days | 90 days | 180 days | 1 year |
cleanup.note: Columns are Canceled / Errored / Pre-Production / Production. Not deleted on PR close: the latest preview for a branch is kept while the branch is active (not deleted, PR not merged/closed). Retention is configurable per team/project.

access.value: Vercel Authentication (all plans); password (Pro add-on); SSO/IPs (Enterprise)
access.quote: Vercel Authentication: Restricts access to only Vercel users with suitable access rights ... Password Protection: ... Available on Pro for $20 per month per protected project ... Trusted IPs: ... Available on the Enterprise plan

license.note: Closed-source commercial managed service; vendor publishes no source code or license for the platform itself (inferred, no explicit license statement fetched).

pricing.value: Unlimited deployments on all plans; Hobby free, Pro $20/mo
pricing.quote: Unlimited Deployments
pricing.note: Pricing page lists Hobby at $0/mo and Pro at $20/mo; 'Unlimited Deployments' shown as Included on Hobby, Pro and Enterprise. Function/compute usage billed per plan.

on_demand_triggers.quote: By default, Vercel creates a preview deployment when you: ... Deploy using the CLI without the `--prod` flag, for example just `vercel`
on_demand_triggers.note: Deploy Hooks: 'Deploy Hooks allow you to create URLs that accept HTTP `POST` requests to trigger deployments ... uniquely linked to your project, repository, and branch' (https://vercel.com/docs/deploy-hooks); a hook on a non-production branch produces a preview. Docs index describes creating 'preview and production deployments on Vercel from Git, Vercel CLI, or the REST API'.

data_copy.quote: Connects your Vercel project to your Neon database to create a database branch for each preview deployment.
data_copy.note: Third-party Marketplace integration (Neon), not a Vercel-native database; Neon branches are copies of the parent DB.

teardown_hooks.quote: deployment.cleanup ... Occurs whenever a deployment is permanently deleted after the recovery period. ... This webhook does not fire immediately when a deployment is marked for deletion
teardown_hooks.note: A notification you must handle yourself (fires after a 30-day recovery period); no built-in pre-delete job or teardown spec.

multi_repo.note: Microfrontends combine separate projects by path routing; a single preview built from several repositories is not documented.

caveats: Previews are protected by 'Standard Protection' scope when enabled; password protection costs $20/month per project on Pro and is unavailable on Hobby (https://vercel.com/docs/deployment-protection).
Pull requests from forks of public repos require authorization from a team member before deploying (https://vercel.com/docs/git).
Hobby teams cannot deploy from private repos in GitHub orgs / GitLab groups / Bitbucket workspaces (https://vercel.com/docs/git).
Neon branching comes from the Neon Marketplace integration, not a built-in Vercel database (https://vercel.com/marketplace/neon).

platforms.name: Netlify
platforms.summary: Managed web platform that automatically builds a Deploy Preview with a unique URL for each pull/merge request (and agent run), including functions, with an on-page feedback drawer.
platforms.summary_short: Deploy Preview per PR for frontends and functions, with a per-preview database branch

scope.value: Frontend + serverless functions (+ Netlify Database branch)
scope.quote: Your functions are version-controlled, built, and deployed along with the rest of your Netlify site, giving you the power of Deploy Previews

hosting.quote: When you open a pull / merge request in a connected site repository from GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Azure DevOps, or Cursor Origin, Netlify automatically builds a Deploy Preview for you.

git.value: GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Azure DevOps, Cursor Origin
git.quote: open pull / merge requests in a connected site repository from GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Azure DevOps, or Cursor Origin.

trigger.value: PR/MR opened; Netlify agent run
trigger.quote: By default, Netlify automatically builds Deploy Previews when you do one of the following: start an agent run...open pull / merge requests in a connected site repository

databases.value: Yes: Netlify Database branch per preview, copied from production
databases.quote: Deploy previews get their own database branch, with a copy of the production data taken when the deploy preview is first created; any changes to the data or the schema made during the lifecycle of the deploy preview will not affect the production database

cleanup.value: Deploys auto-deleted after 30 days (90 on paid); not on PR close
cleanup.quote: By default, Netlify will delete deploys after 30 days (or 90 days on paid plans). This includes deploys triggered by either source control changes, the Netlify UI or CLI, manual uploads, or third-party integrations.
cleanup.note: Enterprise can extend retention up to 365 days. Docs don't state deletion on PR close; database-branch cleanup not documented on the fetched page.

access.value: Password (Pro+); team login/SSO and previews-only scope (Enterprise)
access.quote: Basic password protection for your entire site is available on all Pro plans. All basic password protection and team login protection options are available on Enterprise plans.

license.note: Closed-source commercial managed service; vendor publishes no source code or license for the platform itself (inferred, no explicit license statement fetched).

pricing.value: Unlimited deploy previews on Free; Pro $20/mo
pricing.quote: Unlimited deploy previews
pricing.note: Listed as a Free plan feature; credit-based plans charge 15 credits per production deploy; preview credit cost not stated.

on_demand_triggers.value: Agent run, CLI draft deploy, API, build hook
on_demand_triggers.quote: By default, Netlify automatically builds Deploy Previews when you do one of the following: start an agent run
on_demand_triggers.note: CLI: 'By default, the deploy command deploys to a unique draft URL for previewing and testing.' (https://docs.netlify.com/api-and-cli-guides/cli-guides/get-started-with-cli/). Create-deploys page lists 'API endpoints Create deploys programmatically' and 'Build hooks Trigger deploys from external services using a unique URL' (https://docs.netlify.com/deploy/create-deploys/). Draft/build-hook deploys are draft or branch deploys, not the 'Deploy Preview' type.

data_copy.value: Netlify DB branch with copy of production data
data_copy.quote: Deploy previews get their own database branch, with a copy of the production data taken when the deploy preview is first created; any changes to the data or the schema made during the lifecycle of the deploy preview will not affect the production database

teardown_hooks.quote: Deploy deleted: event emitted when a deploy is manually deleted.
teardown_hooks.note: Notification via HTTP POST outgoing webhook you must handle yourself; not emitted for automatic retention deletion per the wording. No built-in teardown job.

multi_repo.quote: When you open a pull / merge request in a connected site repository from GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Azure DevOps, or Cursor Origin, Netlify automatically builds a Deploy Preview for you.
multi_repo.note: Previews are per connected site repository; found no docs on composing multiple repos into one preview.

caveats: Password protection is not available on credit-based Free and Personal plans (https://docs.netlify.com/manage/security/secure-access-to-sites/password-protection/).
Deploy Previews only build when the PR's base branch is the production branch or has branch deploys enabled (https://docs.netlify.com/deploy/deploy-types/deploy-previews/).
Netlify Database preview branches start as a snapshot of production data, so production data (incl. PII) is copied into previews (https://docs.netlify.com/build/data-and-storage/netlify-db/).

platforms.name: Cloudflare (Pages + Workers Previews)
platforms.summary: Cloudflare Pages creates a preview deployment per branch/PR on pages.dev; Workers (Cloudflare's recommended platform for new projects) has Previews, an isolated per-branch copy of a Worker created with `wrangler preview` or Workers Builds.
platforms.summary_short: Pages preview deployments and Worker Previews per branch/PR

scope.value: Frontend + Workers; per-preview Durable Objects/containers
scope.quote: Cloudflare automatically provisions a new Durable Object namespace and container instances for each Preview. KV, D1, R2, and other resources are isolated when you bind the Preview to a separate resource.

hosting.quote: Previews give each branch an isolated, production-like environment under the same Worker.

git.value: GitHub, GitLab (Pages and Workers Builds); others via CI + Wrangler
git.quote: Cloudflare supports connecting Cloudflare Pages to your GitHub and GitLab repositories. Pages does not currently support connecting self-hosted instances of GitHub or GitLab.
git.note: Workers Builds: 'Workers Builds provides direct integration with Artifacts repositories, GitHub and GitLab accounts.' (https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/ci-cd/builds/git-integration/)

trigger.value: Branch push/PR (Git integration), `wrangler preview`, or CI
trigger.quote: enable Preview Builds and confirm the Preview command is npx wrangler preview. Workers Builds creates the Preview. For GitHub and GitLab repositories, it also comments the Preview URL on the pull request.

databases.value: No auto-provisioned DB; bind D1/KV/R2 per preview manually
databases.quote: Use your base branch to configure one staging database that all Previews share by default. A branch that needs an isolated database overrides that binding in its own configuration.

cleanup.value: Workers: oldest Preview deleted at limit; manual/CI delete. Pages: manual
cleanup.quote: When a limit is reached, Cloudflare automatically deletes the oldest to make room: Preview limit: the Preview that was deployed to least recently is deleted.
cleanup.note: Limits: 100 Previews per Worker on Free, 500 on paid. Docs provide a CI example to delete Previews for closed PRs. Pages: 'To clean up old preview deployments, you can delete them using Wrangler.' (https://developers.cloudflare.com/pages/configuration/preview-deployments/)

access.value: Public by default; Cloudflare Access to require sign-in
access.quote: Preview URLs are public by default. Use Cloudflare Access to require sign-in. You can protect all Previews on an account, one Worker's Previews, or specific hostnames.

license.note: Closed-source commercial managed service; vendor publishes no source code or license for the platform itself (inferred, no explicit license statement fetched). Wrangler CLI is open source (repo metadata not fetched).

pricing.value: Free plan available; Workers Paid from $5/month
pricing.quote: The Workers Paid plan includes Workers, Pages Functions, Workers KV, Hyperdrive, and Durable Objects usage for a minimum charge of $5 USD per month for an account.
pricing.note: Pages static asset requests are free and unlimited on both plans (https://developers.cloudflare.com/pages/functions/pricing/).

on_demand_triggers.value: CLI (wrangler preview / pages deploy --branch), Pages Deploy Hooks, dashboard upload
on_demand_triggers.quote: Running `npx wrangler preview` creates or updates a Preview for your current branch under the same Worker.
on_demand_triggers.note: Pages Deploy Hooks: 'With Deploy Hooks, you can trigger deployments using event sources beyond commits in your source repository' incl. 'Schedule a CRON trigger' (https://developers.cloudflare.com/pages/configuration/deploy-hooks/). Direct Upload: 'npx wrangler pages deploy <OUTPUT_DIRECTORY> --branch=<BRANCH_NAME>' and a dashboard 'Create a new deployment' to preview (https://developers.cloudflare.com/pages/get-started/direct-upload/).

data_copy.value: Shared or separately bound resources only
data_copy.quote: Two Previews bound to the same account-level resource ID or name share its data or instances. Bind a Preview to a different resource to isolate it.
data_copy.note: D1: 'Two Previews sharing the same `database_id` share rows.' Durable Object namespaces are auto-provisioned new per Preview. No documented clone/snapshot of existing data for a Preview.

teardown_hooks.value: Own CI on PR close (documented example)
teardown_hooks.quote: Delete closed pull request Previews ... The workflow trigger above includes the `closed` event. Add this cleanup job under `jobs`:
teardown_hooks.note: Example uses GitHub Actions running `npx wrangler preview delete`; Cloudflare also auto-deletes oldest Previews at limits, with no hook.

multi_repo.quote: Today, if Worker A has a service binding to Worker B and you deploy a Preview of Worker A, the Preview of Worker A can only bind to the production Worker B. It does not automatically bind to a matching Preview of Worker B.
multi_repo.note: Listed under Limitations ('Preview support for these areas may come later').

caveats: Cloudflare now steers new projects to Workers: 'Workers supports most Pages use cases and offers a broader feature set ... Start new projects with Workers.' (https://developers.cloudflare.com/pages/). Pages is not announced as deprecated.

Worker Previews launched in Sept 2026 and require Wrangler 4.135.0+; service bindings, routes and cron triggers from a Preview still target production (https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/previews/).
Cloudflare recommends against using Version URLs / aliased Version URLs for PR previews because they use production resources (https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/previews/compare-workflows/).
Pages PR previews are only created for PRs originating from the repository itself, not forks (https://developers.cloudflare.com/pages/configuration/preview-deployments/).

platforms.name: AWS Amplify Hosting
platforms.feature_name: Web previews for pull requests (fullstack previews)
platforms.summary: AWS-managed hosting that deploys each pull request to a unique preview URL and can optionally create a temporary Amplify backend environment per PR, deleted when the PR closes.
platforms.summary_short: PR previews for frontends/SSR, optionally with a temporary backend per PR

scope.value: Frontend/SSR + optional per-PR Amplify backend
scope.quote: With fullstack previews, you can set up ephemeral fullstack environments on every pull request.

hosting.quote: A web preview deploys every pull request made to your repository to a unique preview URL which is completely different from the URL your main site uses.

git.quote: Amplify supports GitHub, Bitbucket, GitLab, and AWS CodeCommit.

trigger.value: Pull request opened against an enabled branch
trigger.quote: The next time you submit a pull request for the branch, Amplify builds and deploys your PR to a preview URL.

databases.value: Optional temporary backend env per PR (private repos only), or shared
databases.quote: For apps with backend environments provisioned using the Amplify CLI or Amplify Studio, every pull request (private Git repositories only) creates a temporary backend that is deleted when the PR is closed.
databases.note: Alternative option: 'Point all Pull Requests for this branch to an existing environment.' No data seeding documented.

cleanup.value: Yes, preview and backend deleted on PR close
cleanup.quote: After the pull request is closed, the preview URL is deleted, and any temporary backend environment linked to the pull request is deleted.

access.value: Basic-auth username/password per branch or app-wide
access.quote: When access control is set on a branch, users are prompted for a user name and password when they attempt to access the URL for the branch.

license.note: Closed-source commercial managed service; vendor publishes no source code or license for the platform itself (inferred, no explicit license statement fetched).

pricing.value: Pay-as-you-go (build $0.01/min); 12-month free tier
pricing.quote: No cost up to 1,000 build minutes per month
pricing.note: Free tier is 'Free for 12 months.' Standard build instance '$0.01 per minute'. Per-PR backends incur the underlying AWS resource costs.

on_demand_triggers.quote: CreateBranch Creates a new branch for an Amplify app.
on_demand_triggers.note: StartJob: 'Starts a new job for a branch of an Amplify app.' (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amplify/latest/APIReference/API_StartJob.html). PR web previews themselves are PR-only: 'A web preview deploys every pull request made to your repository to a unique preview URL' (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amplify/latest/userguide/pr-previews.html). Incoming webhooks rebuild an existing branch. Debatable: could be scored 'no' for PR previews.

data_copy.value: New temporary backend or shared dev backend
data_copy.quote: For example, you might want all your preview branches to point to the backend resources deployed by the dev branch so you can reuse seed data, users, and groups.
data_copy.note: Otherwise each PR gets a fresh 'temporary backend that is deleted when the PR is closed' (userguide pr-previews). No documented data clone.

teardown_hooks.value: Auto-delete only; no custom hook documented
teardown_hooks.quote: After the pull request is closed, the preview URL is deleted, and any temporary backend environment linked to the pull request is deleted.
teardown_hooks.note: Automatic teardown of Amplify-managed resources; no documentation of running custom cleanup steps.

multi_repo.value: Frontend repo points at backend from another repo
multi_repo.quote: You might have different frontend and backend teams that maintain their own repositories. With Amplify Gen 2, you can deploy repositories that have backend-only code, so frontend and backend teams can operate independently of each other.
multi_repo.note: Frontend build runs `npx ampx generate outputs --branch main --app-id <your-backend-app-id>`, i.e. it targets a fixed backend branch, not a per-PR backend built from the other repo.

caveats: Each PR counts toward the quota of 50 branches per app (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amplify/latest/userguide/pr-previews.html).

Previews cannot be enabled for public repos on apps needing an IAM service role (backends, WEB_COMPUTE/SSR) to prevent untrusted code running with your role (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amplify/latest/userguide/pr-previews.html).
GitHub previews require the Amplify GitHub App; OAuth-connected apps must migrate first (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amplify/latest/userguide/pr-previews.html).

platforms.name: Azure Static Web Apps
platforms.summary: Azure service for static frontends with managed Azure Functions APIs; its generated GitHub Actions workflow deploys each pull request to a staging environment that is deleted when the PR closes.
platforms.summary_short: Staging environment per PR for static sites and managed Functions APIs

scope.value: Static frontend + managed Azure Functions APIs
scope.quote: | APIs via Azure Functions | Managed | Managed or Bring your own Functions app |

hosting.quote: A pre-production environment is a fully functional staged version of your application that includes changes not available in production.

git.value: GitHub (Actions) only for auto PR envs; Azure DevOps manual
git.quote: Pull request environments are not automatically supported for Azure DevOps, but you can use named environments to set them up manually.
git.note: Limitations section: 'Only GitHub Actions deployments support pre-production environments.'

trigger.value: PR against a watched branch (GitHub Actions workflow)
trigger.quote: Azure Static Web Apps generates a YAML workflow in the repo. When a pull request is created against a branch that the workflow watches, the pre-production environment gets built.

databases.note: No per-preview database documented. The Database Connections feature is retired: 'Retirement notice: Database Connections for Static Web Apps ends November 30, 2025.' (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/static-web-apps/database-overview)

cleanup.value: Yes, deleted when PR closes
cleanup.quote: The lifecycle of a pre-production environment is tied to the pull request. Once the pull request is closed, the pre-production environment is automatically deleted.

access.value: Public by default; password for staging (Standard plan)
access.quote: select Protect staging environments only to protect only your app's pre-production environments or select Protect both production and staging environments to protect all environments.
access.note: Prerequisite: 'An existing static web app in the Standard plan.' PR docs warn: 'Anyone can access the staged versions of your application via their URL, even if your GitHub repo is private.'

license.note: Service itself is closed-source; only the GitHub Action repo carries an MIT license.

pricing.value: Free plan (3 staging envs); Standard (10 staging envs)
pricing.quote: | Staging environments | 3 per app | 10 per app | 20 per app |
pricing.note: Columns: Free / Standard / Dedicated (retired). Standard price not rendered in fetched pricing page text; see https://azure.microsoft.com/pricing/details/app-service/static/.

on_demand_triggers.quote: --env [environment] : the type of deployment environment where to deploy the project (default: " preview ")
on_demand_triggers.note: Named environments exist but are driven by your CI pipeline config ('Set the `deployment_environment` input...'), not a separate platform trigger. PR environments are created by the generated GitHub Actions workflow, so any GitHub trigger can be added by the user.

data_copy.quote: Retirement notice: Database Connections for Static Web Apps ends November 30, 2025.
data_copy.note: Only database feature was connections to an existing DB (now retired); nothing about cloning data for pre-production environments.

teardown_hooks.quote: close_pull_request_job: if: github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.action == 'closed' runs-on: ubuntu-latest name: Close Pull Request Job steps: - name: Close Pull Request id: closepullrequest uses: Azure/static-web-apps-deploy@v1 with: ... action: "close"
teardown_hooks.note: Quote is from the YAML sample on the page (newlines collapsed, token line elided with '...'). The job runs in your own GitHub Actions, so extra cleanup steps can be added there.

multi_repo.value: Linked backends not allowed on PR environments
multi_repo.quote: Bring your own API backends cannot be linked to a Static Web Apps pull request environment.
multi_repo.note: Container Apps page: 'Backend integration is not supported on Static Web Apps pull request environments.'

caveats: Pre-production environments aren't geo-distributed (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/static-web-apps/review-publish-pull-requests).
The Dedicated plan was retired effective October 31, 2025 (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/static-web-apps/plans).
Database Connections (Data API builder) feature retired November 30, 2025 (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/static-web-apps/database-overview).
Azure/static-web-apps-deploy repo last pushed 2024-09-11 (GitHub API).

platforms.name: Firebase Hosting
platforms.summary: Google's static/web hosting where `firebase hosting:channel:deploy` or the official GitHub Action deploys to a temporary preview channel URL that expires after a TTL; previews talk to the project's real backend.
platforms.summary_short: Temporary preview channels for static sites, using the live backend

scope.value: Static frontend; uses the project's live backend
scope.quote: Reminder: When using preview URLs, your app interacts with the real backend resources of your Firebase project.

hosting.quote: If you need your teammates to view and test your changes, Hosting can create sharable, temporary preview URLs for your site.

git.value: GitHub (via official GitHub Action); any CI via CLI
git.quote: Creates a new preview channel (and its associated preview URL) for every PR on your GitHub repository.

trigger.value: CLI command or GitHub Action on PR commits
trigger.quote: firebase hosting:channel:deploy CHANNEL_ID
trigger.note: 'Firebase Hosting supports a GitHub Action that automatically creates and updates a preview URL when you commit changes to a pull request.'

databases.quote: Reminder: When using preview URLs, your app interacts with the real backend resources of your Firebase project.

cleanup.value: Yes, TTL: expires after 7 days by default (max 30)
cleanup.quote: By default, a preview channel expires 7 days from its creation date, but your site's live channel will never expire. When a preview channel expires, the channel, along with its releases and associated versions, are scheduled for deletion within 24 hours.
cleanup.note: 'The expiration can be up to 30 days from the date of deploy.' Not tied to PR close.

access.value: Public (unguessable URL), no built-in protection
access.quote: Note that although preview URLs are difficult to guess (as they contain a random hash), they are public. So, anyone who knows the URL can access it.

license.note: Service itself is closed-source; the deploy Action is Apache-2.0.

pricing.value: No-cost Spark plan (10 GB storage); Blaze pay-as-you-go
pricing.quote: No-cost up to 10 GB
pricing.note: Hosting storage on Spark plan; Blaze 'Then $0.026/GB'. Data transfer: 'No-cost up to 360 MB/day', then '$0.15/GB'.

on_demand_triggers.quote: From the root of your local project directory, run the following command: firebase hosting:channel:deploy CHANNEL_ID
on_demand_triggers.note: REST: 'Creates a new channel in the specified site.' (https://firebase.google.com/docs/reference/hosting/rest/v1beta1/sites.channels/create).

data_copy.quote: When using a preview URL, your web app interacts with your real backend for all project resources (with the exception of any "pinned" functions in your rewrites config).

teardown_hooks.quote: When a preview channel expires, the channel, along with its releases and associated versions, are scheduled for deletion within 24 hours.
teardown_hooks.note: Also 'firebase hosting:channel:delete CHANNEL_ID'. No documented custom cleanup hook.

multi_repo.quote: (Optional) Deploys the current state of your GitHub repo to your live channel when the PR is merged.

trigger.quote: Harbor seamlessly leverages GitHub Actions to provision a dedicated site on the Laravel Forge server.

cleanup.value: Yes, teardown workflow on PR merge/close
cleanup.quote: Running the harbor teardown removes the previously created task scheduler, database, database user, and finally, the site for the related site on Forge.

pricing.note: Pricing isn't documented. The tool is MIT; it needs a Laravel Forge account and servers, which are billed by Forge and your host.

caveats: Laravel/PHP-specific and needs Laravel Forge.

platforms.name: GitLab Review Apps
platforms.summary: GitLab CI/CD feature built on dynamic environments: a pipeline job deploys each branch/MR to infrastructure you supply, and GitLab tracks the environment, links it in the MR and runs stop jobs.
platforms.summary_short: Dynamic environment per MR, with stop jobs and auto-stop

scope.value: Whatever your CI deploy job deploys
scope.quote: You must set up the infrastructure to host and deploy the review apps.

hosting.value: Your own infrastructure (Kubernetes via Auto DevOps optional)
hosting.quote: If you have a Kubernetes cluster, you can set up review apps automatically using Auto DevOps.

git.quote: Review apps are temporary testing environments that are created automatically for each branch or merge request.

trigger.value: CI pipeline per branch or merge request
trigger.quote: Built on dynamic environments, review apps provide a unique environment for each branch or merge request.

databases.note: No built-in per-review-app database. Your deploy scripts would have to provision one.

cleanup.value: Yes, stop job on MR merge/close; auto_stop_in TTL
cleanup.quote: After the time period passes, GitLab automatically starts a job to stop the environment.
cleanup.note: Also: "When you use the merge request pipelines configuration, the `stop` trigger is automatically enabled."

access.note: No built-in URL protection documented for review apps. It depends on your hosting.

license.quote: All content that resides under the "ee/" directory of this repository, if that directory exists, is licensed under the license defined in "ee/LICENSE".

pricing.value: Available on Free, Premium, Ultimate tiers
pricing.quote: Tier: Free, Premium, Ultimate

caveats: GitLab orchestrates; it doesn't host. You write the deploy and stop jobs yourself (https://docs.gitlab.com/ci/review_apps/).

platforms.name: GitHub Actions deployment environments
platforms.summary: GitHub's environments track deployments and gate jobs with protection rules. They're a building block for PR previews, but don't provision or host anything.
platforms.summary_short: Deployment tracking, protection rules and scoped secrets; you provision the preview

scope.value: None itself; tracks deployments your workflow performs
scope.quote: Environments are used to describe a general deployment target like `production`, `staging`, or `development`.

hosting.note: No hosting. You deploy to your own infrastructure or a third-party platform from the workflow.

git.quote: When a workflow references an environment, the environment will appear in the repository's deployments.

trigger.value: Workflow referencing an environment (auto-created)
trigger.quote: Running a workflow that references an environment that does not exist will create an environment with the referenced name.

cleanup.note: No automatic per-PR environment deletion documented. You can delete environments manually or via the API.

access.note: Protection rules gate deployments, not preview URL access.

license.quote: Users with GitHub Free plans can only configure environments for public repositories.
license.note: No license statement on the page. The proprietary value reflects that GitHub is a commercial SaaS; the quote shows plan gating.

pricing.value: Free plans: public repos only; Pro/Team for private
pricing.quote: Organizations with GitHub Team and users with GitHub Pro can configure environments for private repositories.

caveats: This isn't a preview-environment system. Teams combine it with a hosting target and their own create/teardown jobs.

platforms.name: Azure Pipelines Review App (Kubernetes environments)
platforms.summary: Azure Pipelines can deploy each pull request into a dynamically created Kubernetes namespace resource in an environment and comment the review app link on GitHub.
platforms.summary_short: Deploys each PR to a dynamically created Kubernetes namespace

scope.value: Kubernetes manifests deployed to a per-PR namespace
scope.quote: The review app deploys every pull request from your Git repository to a dynamic Kubernetes resource in the environment, and posts a GitHub comment linking to the review app.

hosting.quote: You can connect to public or private Kubernetes clusters in Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) or other cloud providers.

git.value: PRs from your Git repo; GitHub comment documented
git.quote: The review app deploys every pull request from your Git repository to a dynamic Kubernetes resource in the environment, and posts a GitHub comment linking to the review app.

trigger.value: Pipeline run on PR create/update
trigger.quote: The second job runs when a PR is created or updated to the `main` branch, and deploys against a dynamic review app resource it creates in the cluster on demand.

cleanup.note: No automatic namespace cleanup is documented on this page.

access.note: Not documented. The example exposes a LoadBalancer IP.

license.note: Closed-source commercial service; no open-source license is published (inferred).

pricing.value: Billed as Azure Pipelines parallel jobs; free tier
pricing.quote: 1 free parallel job with 1,800 minutes

caveats: Set up through the 'Deploy to Azure Kubernetes Services' template's 'Enable Review App flow for Pull Requests' option (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/pipelines/process/environments-kubernetes).
